  MEETING OF THE
  PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION
  MONDAY, JULY 18, 2022 AT 6:00 P.M.
  VIA TELECONFERENCE

The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Community interest provides the Public
Safety Commission with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular meetings are held on the 3rd Monday of every month.

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who requires
a reasonable modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact
the Public Safety Commission via email at fire@cityofsanmarino.org or by phone at (626) 300-
0735 prior to the meeting for assistance.

  PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361 (AB 361)
Members of the Public Safety Commission may teleconference into the meeting without noticing
each teleconference location from which a member will be participating in a public meeting.

  CORONAVIRUS DISEASE (COVID-19) ADVISORY
As a precaution to protect staff, our constituents, and appointed officials, the City is following
the State and County Health Department’s current Health Officer recommendations to prevent
and reduce transmission of COVID0-19 by holding meetings via teleconference

Members of the public may observe and offer comment at this meeting telephonically or
otherwise electronically:

  1) Public comment will be accepted by email to fire@cityofsanmarino.org before or during
  the meeting, prior to the close of public comment on an item, to be read by the
  Committee during public comment. Lengthy public comment may be summarized in the
  interest of time.

FROM:  John N. Incontro, Police Chief

DATE:  July 18, 2022

SUBJECT:  POLICE DEPARTMENT UPDATE REPORT JUNE 2022

BACKGROUND

Each month, the San Marino Police Department provides a brief and informational update on
crime, traffic issues, and other items of interest to the public and to the Public Safety Committee.

DISCUSSION

This report is compiled in order to inform the Public Safety Commission with essential
information regarding the department’s activity in the month of June 2022.

Detective Bureau / Investigations

As of June 1, 2022, the Detective Bureau completed the following activities:

•  5 filings were submitted to the district attorney’s office for review
•  One search warrant for three communication devices was authored for an on-going
residential burglary investigation

In June of 2022, there were a total of four residential burglaries. Two of these residences had an
alarm activated and surveillance cameras operating. However, at one residence the alarm
activation triggered but an activation notification was never received by the police department
from the alarm company. One residence had two separate burglaries occur. Due to a recent fire,
the utilities were all shut off at this location prior to when the burglaries occurred.

In early June, officers responded to a report of a burglary in-progress call. Dispatch originally
received an audible alarm activation from the alarm company for the residence. Moments later,
the resident remotely observed suspects inside the home through surveillance camera video.
The surveillance cameras captured four suspects on the property. The suspects smashed a
bathroom window to gain entry inside the home. Patrol officers quickly responded to set up a
containment in the area to locate the suspect(s). Detectives also responded to the area to assist
patrol officers with the containment. The detectives were on their way to assist when they

  Page 7 of 34
 observed a van leaving the immediate area at a high rate of speed. Detectives conducted a traffic
enforcement stop on the van. The van failed to yield and a pursuit ensued.

After a short pursuit, the vehicle collided into a stop sign in the City of San Gabriel. The driver
was immediately taken into custody. A second containment was set up for an outstanding suspect
fleeing the van. Officers were able to locate a second suspect who fled on foot from the van.
Detectives worked with an L.A. County law enforcement task force and discovered these
individuals were part of a Chilean burglary crew targeting jewelry store owners in multiple cities.
Detectives contacted known San Marino residents who own prominent jewelry stores in an effort
to educate these individuals by providing safety tips.

Our analysis indicates that there is no specific pattern or location selected for the above incidents.
The point of entry for these incidents was the rear of the home. This information will assist us
in our crime prevention efforts. We have provided the information to residents via the
Neighborhood Watch Block Captains, police department website, e-mail and social media.
Additionally, we are working on a crime suppression strategy to reduce these crimes.

During this month, there were 41 FLOCK Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) stolen vehicle
notifications. These notifications included misreads or vehicles not removed from the stolen
vehicle database by the originating agency. Officers pursued each notification as a possible stolen
vehicle and searched the area. Two suspects were apprehended with the assistance of the FLOCK
cameras. A short pursuit ensued with one of the stolen vehicles into the City of Pasadena. A
containment was set up and the suspect was located while running out of the yard where the
containment was set.

The FLOCK cameras are not only a useful tool to locate stolen vehicles but have helped with
follow up investigations. Officers and Detectives are able to locate suspect vehicles by searching
vehicle images through the FLOCK database. In late June, Officers were investigating a road rage
and battery incident. The driver of the suspect vehicle was driving erratically and ended up
throwing a cup of coffee threw the victim’s driver side window. Officers were able to locate the
suspect vehicle with the help of the FLOCK cameras.

  Page 8 of 34
 Community Engagement

The month of June was spent preparing for our largest community events, Fourth of July and
National Night Out. Officer Ernesto Lopez was introduced to the neighborhood block captains
this month. The department will be hosting “Cone with a Cop” at Swirlz on July 28th from 2-5
PM. We purchased a corn toss set that will be used for upcoming events. There will potentially
be a community/department tournament at National Night Out.

Personnel

The department currently has all 30 sworn positions filled. We continue to actively pursue
interested police officer applicants, in the event a vacancy arises. There are still three cadet
position vacancies. We expect to hold interviews in the coming weeks, and hope to fill a couple
of the cadet positions.

Technology

Our Flock cameras continue to be a success with locating would be criminals traveling through
the City of San Marino. They have also assisted our officers and detectives in multiple
investigations. They have helped solve crimes within the city, as well as link the suspects to crimes
occurring in other jurisdictions. We are also in the process of researching other technology to
help our Officers investigate traffic and crime scenes. We also hope to purchase additional
automated defibrillator devices for additional police fleet vehicles and the station.

Traffic

The Office of Traffic Safety grant requires the department to conduct a number of traffic safety
operations during the grant period, and they provide the funding for the event. On Saturday,
June 2nd, members of the San Marino Police Department, in collaboration with police officers
from the South Pasadena Police Department, conducted a traffic detail. San Marino Officers held
a click it or ticket detail as well as a traffic enforcement detail during the month of June.

  Page 9 of 34
 Traffic Enforcement

Traffic enforcement is based upon three categories; traffic complaints from the community,
observation of violations by officers, and traffic collision data. The Department maintains a list of
traffic complaint locations and traffic collision data for traffic enforcement. As part of our traffic
collision investigations, we will look for other issues that may have been a contributory factor in
the collision. Those factors could be distracted driving, engineering, or environmental.

Below are the top collision locations of June 2022

  1.  Huntington Drive - Three Collisions
  2.  San Marino Avenue - Three Collisions
  2.  Monterey Road - Two Collisions
  3.  Kenilworth Avenue - Two Collisions
  4.  San Gabriel Boulevard - One Collision
  5.  Oxford Road - One Collision
  6.  Avonrea Road - One Collision

Below are the top factors of collisions of June 2022

  1.  CVC 22107 - Turning and Stopping and Turning Signals – Four Collisions
  2.  CVC 21453(a) - Failure to stop at red light – One Collison
  3.  CVC 21800(a)- Failure to yield – One Collison
  4.  CVC 22350 - Speeding – Five Collisions
  5.  Unknown causes - One Collision

Moving Violations

The patrol division is continuing maximum education/enforcement efforts in place of the vacant
motor officer positions. They try to respond to all traffic complaints and address the primary
collision areas.

 Radar Trailer

The department’s radar trailer did not collect data for the month of June. As of July 12, 2022 we
have had the trailer serviced and it is up and running.

Radar Deployment Locations:

  •  980 Huntington Drive (E/B traffic)
  •  Sierra Madre / Huntley (S/B traffic)

FROM:  M. D. Rueda, Fire Chief

DATE:  June 20, 2022

SUBJECT:  FIRE DEPARTMENT MONTHLY REPORT

BACKGROUND

The San Marino Fire Department completes a monthly report for the Public Safety Commission,
providing an overview of department activities, significant incidents, and monthly statistics.

DISCUSSION

Personnel
Since the last meeting of the Public Safety Commission, the Fire Department has completed
orientation for the two firefighter recruits hired in April 2022. The probationary firefighters
began their first shift rotations on May 6 and May 8. The Fire Department currently has no vacant
positions.

Overtime hours decreased in May 2022 as a result of the decreased vacant position coverage.
The remaining overtime hours were largely due to injury on duty coverage at the
Firefighter/Paramedic and Shared Division Chief ranks

Annual Brush Inspections
The Fire Department completed initial brush inspections of properties located in the Very High
Fire Hazard Severity Zone. Generally, residents are extremely cooperative in complying with
the annual notices to clear their hazardous vegetation; however, the Fire Department did issue
13 violation notices during this year’s inspections. Reinspections of properties that were given
violation notices for hazardous conditions have been scheduled for 30 days after the initial
inspection. The Fire Department conducts annual inspections to ensure the safety of lives and
properties in the hillside community. Property owners in the Very High Fire Hazard Severity
Zone were notified by mail of the upcoming inspections at the beginning of May. Notifications
included a checklist of common hazardous conditions that the Fire Department will be inspecting.
More information on the San Marino Fire Department’s brush clearance program may be found
at www.cityofsanmarino.org/brushclearance.

  Page 15 of 34
 Annual Department Inspections
Annual inspections of the Fire Department facilities and equipment were conducted in May.
Annual Inspections are conducted by the respective shifts assigned Division Chief. Each shift is
assigned an area of responsibility for cleaning, maintenance, and repair (e.g. fire station quarters,
apparatus and equipment, or facility exteriors) in addition to each firefighter’s personal
equipment, documentation, and training records.

First Aid & Summer Safety Course
The San Marino Fire Department hosted a First Aid & Summer Safety class on Monday, May 23.
Attendees of the class were taught first aid skills, including CPR, active bleeding, the use of
tourniquets; use of fire extinguishers; and pool and water safety. The Fire Department plans to
conduct two more safety workshops this year. Many of the attendees for this event were
students from our San Marino schools that attended with their parents.

Emergency Management Training
City of San Marino executive staff attend monthly emergency management training coordinated
by the San Marino Fire Department. In May, the Fire Department invited representatives from
the Los Angeles County Department of Public Health’s Radiation Management Program to
present a workshop on Nuclear Detonation: Blas Characteristics & Sheltering in Place Guidance.
The workshop included a simulated detonation of a 10-kiloton nuclear weapon in Los Angeles.
The workshop reviewed the characteristics of a nuclear detonation, damage zones and expected
casualties, overview of the three actions to be performed following a nuclear detonation, a review

  Page 16 of 34
 of protection factors for determining safe shelter locations, and response after a nuclear
detonation.

Fire Department Recognized for COVID-19 Response
On May 18, the Los Angeles County Department of Public Health recognized the San Marino
Fire Department for the sacrifices of emergency medical services personnel to ensure a safe
environment during the COVID-19 pandemic. The certificate was accepted by Captain Jason
Sutliff, who has managed the Emergency Operations Center since the beginning of the pandemic,
and has been essential in the City’s COVID-19 response.

Fourth of July
As part of the preparations for this year’s 4th of July event, the San Marino Fire Department
prepared a tabletop exercise for executive level personnel on a potential multi-casualty incident
occurring at the Lacy Park venue. Executive staff was guided through the scenario and prompted
to describe their actions for each inject, such as initial response (triage, crowd control,
evacuation, etc.), establishment of a family assistance center, debriefing of elected officials, media
response, and long-term response (logistical support and clean up, mental health support,
memorials, criminal prosecutions, etc.). Though it is our hope that no similar incident would
ever occur in our community, it is the duty of City staff to be prepared for any potential event
that may affect the safety of our residents.

Significant Incidents
On June 2, the San Marino Fire Department, along with mutual aid assistance from the Pasadena
Fire Department, responded to a structure fire involving a 3,000 square foot, one story home on
California Boulevard. Engine 91 discovered a large fire showing from an attached garage,
spreading into the residence. The fire was described as oven-like conditions at the rear of the
home by firefighters. As a result of a quick attack on the fire, the fire was extinguished in
approximately 20 minutes. The occupants escaped the home and met firefighters upon their
arrival. There were no injuries, and the fire was contained to the garage and the rear kitchen
portion of the home. The cause is under investigation. San Marino Police Department assisted
with crowd and traffic control.

Following the incident, San Marino Fire Department personnel went door to door in the
surrounding neighborhood to inspect residents’ smoke alarms and provide/install free smoke
alarms where they were missing/non-operational. The San Marino Fire Department provides
smoke alarm inspections as part of Operation: Fire Safe. Operation: Fire Safe is a voluntary
program intended to teach San Marino residents the dangers of fire and how to prevent them.
During an Operation: Fire Safe inspection, Fire Department personnel will inspect your home for
fire hazards and provide recommendations to help decrease fire risk. Information about
Operation: Fire Safe, including brochures and a home survey checklist are available on our
website at www.cityofsanmarino.org/operationfiresafe. Residents may schedule an Operation:
Fire Safe inspection by contacting (626) 300-0735 or emailing fire@cityofsanmarino.org.

  Page 17 of 34
 On Monday, June 27 Engine 91 and Battalion 9 responded with the Los Angeles County Fire
Department to a two-story home on fire on Hidden Pine Drive adjacent to San Marino in San
Gabriel. E91 assisted with attacking the fire on the second story. E91 personnel depleted two
sets of air cylinders during the fire attack. All firefighters were evacuated from the interior
prior to the collapse of a significant portion of the roof. No San Marino firefighters sustained
injuries during the incident. Outside temperatures throughout the duration of the incident
were between 96 – 100 degrees.

FY 2022-23 Department Objectives
  • Complete the Lexipol implementation of fire department policies and procedures.
  • Accept delivery of the new RA 91.
  • Conduct a review of the current Community Emergency Response Training (CERT) and
  develop a “Citizen Fire Academy” for residents’ participation.
  • Conduct Fire Department First Aid Community Instructional Workshops.
  • Begin construction on the Fire Department’s bathroom renovation.
  • Develop and conduct emergency operations, active shooter training partnered with a
  consultant and the Huntington Library staff.
  • Present the City’s revised Emergency Operations Plan to the Disaster Council and City
  Council for approval.
  • Update the City’s Disaster Cache Inventory.
  • Complete the EOC upgrade.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends the Commission receive and file the Fire Department Monthly Report. If the
Commission concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

“I move to receive and file the Fire Department Monthly Report.”

FROM:  M. D. Rueda, Fire Chief

DATE:  July 7, 2022

SUBJECT:  FIRE DEPARTMENT MONTHLY PERFORMANCE REPORT

The attached San Marino Fire Department June 2022 Performance Report represents the incident
data reports intended to meet the Improvement Goals referenced in the March 2, 2018 Report
to City Council titled; Implementation Plan Fire Department Deployment Study. The Fire
Department has been working closely with the Verdugo Fire Communications Center (Verdugo)
to ensure the accuracy of the data being reported. Some of the data sets are not currently
available from Verdugo and are listed as N/A. Verdugo has been made aware of the San Marino
Fire Department’s interest in pursuing the data associated with the fire and life safety goals as
approved by the City Council.

Improvement Goal A in the Report recommended the following:

Call Processing Goals
9-1-1 calls will be answered at the primary PSAP (Public Safety Answering Point) San Marino
Police Department within 15 seconds, 95% of the time.

9-1-1 calls will be transferred from the primary PSAP to Verdugo within 30 seconds from the
time answered, 95% of the time.
This data is not available.

Recommended Turnout Goal
Response personnel shall initiate the response of a unit capable of mitigating an incident to a
priority fire and rescue incident 80 seconds from notification 90% of the time.

Response personnel shall initiate response to all other priority incidents within 60 seconds from
notification 90% of the time.

Recommended First-Due Response Time Goal
The first response unit capable of initiating effective incident intervention shall arrive at a priority
fire or rescue incident within 5 minutes and 20 seconds from notification of response personnel,
90 percent of the time.

  Page 19 of 34
 The first response unit capable of initiating effective incident intervention shall arrive at all other
priority incidents within 5 minutes from notification of response personnel, 90% of the time.

Recommended Response Force Goal
The full effective response force shall arrive at a moderate risk structure fire within 9 minutes
and 20 seconds of notification of response personnel, 90% of the time.
This data is not available.

Cardiac Arrest Data
The Cardiac Arrest data set includes the total number of cardiac arrest patients treated by
Firefighter/Paramedics. We always pray that the number is as low as possible. The more
important data sets are the subsequent measures which include the number of times the
Firefighter/Paramedics are successful in returning a patient’s spontaneous circulation (ROSC) –
our goal with ROSC is always 100%. Saving lives is why the Fire Department exists; unfortunately,
this is not always in our control. Lastly, the subsequent data sets measure the percentages of
correct treatments performed by the Firefighter/Paramedics.

 TO:  Chair Boozell and members of the Public Safety Commission

FROM:  Robert Newman, Interim Director of Parks & Public Works/City Engineer

DATE:  July 18, 2022

SUBJECT:  JUNE THROUGH JULY PARKS AND PUBLIC WORKS UPDATE

BACKGROUND

Please accept the following as a summary of notable activities that have been accomplished, are
underway or are planned for the balance of this month through your next regularly scheduled
commission meeting.

DISCUSSION

Follow-up Items from Prior Commission Meetings
•  Striping modifications on Huntington Drive westbound between Monterey Road and
  Westhaven Road is still under review by the City’s traffic engineer. A design is expected to
  be shared with the Commission at a future meeting.
•  Iteris is working to complete its Citywide traffic circulation study, including incorporating
  residential survey results, improvement prioritization, and additional conceptual designs for
  the intersection of Huntington Drive at Sierra Madre Boulevard/San Marino Avenue. Staff
  recently met with Iteris to get a progress update. During this meeting, they indicated that
  they anticipate this study will be ready to share with the Commission in the late summer/early
  fall.
•  The traffic concerns raised by residents on Bellhaven Road at a previous Commission meeting
  is still pending. Staff is recommending this be addressed after the Citywide Traffic Circulation
  Study is approved by City Council.

Projects in or near Construction
•  Mariposa Landscaping has continued its scheduled work in its Multi-Year Tree Maintenance
  Contract for FY 22-23. To this point, they have planted approximately 70 new trees at
  various locations throughout the City, performed removal of trees approved by the City
  Council, trimmed palm trees citywide, and trimmed trees at Lacy Park in preparation for the

  Page 25 of 34
   4th of July celebration. They are also currently performing grid trimming of right-of-way trees
  south of Huntington Drive from Del Mar Avenue westbound to City limits.
•  Thermoplastic striping in the form of a ladder-pattern crosswalk was installed at the
  intersection of Lorain Road and West Drive to help improve pedestrian safety by making the
  crosswalk more apparent to motorists. Additional striping, including lane separators and
  raised pavement markers (RPM’s) were also installed at the intersection of Darby Road and
  Granada Avenue, as well as Roxbury Road and Granada Avenue. These measures will help
  improve both traffic and pedestrian safety at the busy intersection.
•  Construction for this fiscal year’s street rehabilitation program project is currently scheduled
  to begin in August. A total of 31 City streets are scheduled to be resurfaced based on the
  Council-adopted pavement management plan. The restriping work on Sierra Madre Boulevard
  be previously discussed at a Commission meeting has been incorporated into the project’s
  scope of work.
•  Construction for the FY 22-23 sidewalk replacement program is expected to begin in the fall.
  This program replaces approximately 1.0 mile of sidewalk each year at various locations
  throughout the City.
Items for City Council

•  Award of construction contract for the San Marino Center will be brought to the City Council
  at their July 29th meeting. Should the City Council approve the award of contract, construction
  is expected to begin in September.
Projects in Design/Out-to-Bid

•  City staff and the architect continued to work with the San Marino Center (SMC) community
  task force on detailed design work to renovate SMC into a new community facility. At its June
  8 meeting, the City Council approved the certification of the project’s Environmental Impact
  Report. The report can be accessed at
  https://www.cityofsanmarino.org/government/departments/community_development/san_m
  arino_center_renovation.php

  In addition, the Council authorized Public Works to advertise the project for construction
  bids. Award of construction contract is expected to be brought before the Council at its July
  29th meeting.

•  The Department received a request to study the signage on West Drive at Sherwood Road
  and at Lorain Road for the purposes of highlighting pedestrian activity at these intersections.
  The Department has updated several signs with the current labeling and colors for signs and
  has completed the refreshing of existing ladder crosswalk striping in the near future.

•  Dudek engineers continue to work on the plans to upgrade of our 3 sanitary sewer lift stations
  as part of the lift station improvement program. They are at the 95% design plans stage.
  Advertisement for construction bids is planned for later this year.
